population.note: FICTIONAL ESTIMATES. ~262M US adults × 17.1% ≈ 44.8M current users. Age check: 0.20×9 + 0.33×17 + 0.24×27 + 0.23×14 ≈ 17.1. Income thirds average (21.0+15.6+14.7)/3 ≈ 17.1. The middle third has the slowest growth: employer coverage left it, and it earns too much for the $0-copay public tier. Cycling arithmetic: ever 23.5 − current 17.1 = 6.4% of adults used and are off now. About 7.0 points of the 17.1 current users are restarters, consistent with ~35% one-year persistence and 36–47% restart among stoppers across three years of cohorts. Another ~0.6 points of the off-now group restarted once and then stopped again. (7.0+0.6)/23.5 ≈ 32% of ever-users have cycled off and on. The 65+ band rose from 9 to 14 on the Medicare Bridge successor and $0 low-income copays, and it is the band where the muscle–bone signal sits. Pediatric: ~0.4% of all under-18s (about a quarter of those with obesity are aged 12+ with a prescription event). Upper-income children are still ~50% more likely to be prescribed. Never-able-to-afford: an estimated 9–11M adults with BMI≥30 and no diabetes code sit in the middle-income, employer-dropped tier. They have no coverage and do not qualify for public subsidy. This group makes up most of the gray-market buyers.

access.public_coverage: Medicare: the GLP-1 Bridge pilot expired Dec 2027. It was succeeded by a CMMI 'Metabolic Health' model (Jan 2028–Dec 2030), with the negotiated price stepped down from $245 to $219/month. The standard copay stays $50. Copay is $0 for Part D Low-Income Subsidy enrollees and for adult Medicaid in participating states (31 states + DC). Model eligibility requires a baseline DEXA scan for 65+ and documented resistance-training/protein counselling. Arithmetic: ~3.4M Medicare obesity-indication users × $219 × 12 ≈ $8.9B/yr gross. ~2.6M Medicaid obesity-indication users × $219 × 12 ≈ $6.8B/yr (federal share ~$4.6B at ~68% blended FMAP). The LIS copay waiver costs ~1.2M users × $50 × 12 ≈ $0.72B/yr. Separately, Ozempic/Wegovy/Rybelsus carry the IRA negotiated Medicare price ($274) for diabetes use from 2027. State: New Jersey's problem-gambling fund pays for an off-label pilot, ~4,000 participants × $199 × 12 ≈ $9.6M/yr.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India: 60+ generic semaglutide brands at ~$8–48/month; oral generics launched 2027. Canada: generic semaglutide ~CAD 70–110/month, widely used by US border-state residents. Brazil, Mexico, Turkey and much of Southeast Asia have generics; ~160 countries have access. China: domestic long-acting GLP-1s, including a monthly depot approved Jan 2028. Tirzepatide is still branded everywhere.
access.note: Payer mix of ~44.8M users: Medicare ~8.4M (≈5.0M diabetes/CV codes + 3.4M obesity), Medicaid ~5.0M (2.4M diabetes + 2.6M obesity), employer/commercial ~17.4M (most now coded diabetes, CV, OSA or MASH), cash ~14.0M. Of the cash users, ~10.5M use manufacturer-direct/TrumpRx and ~3.5M use the gray market (~8% of all users). Cash prices: Wegovy pill and Foundayo starter doses $149, maintenance doses $199–299. Injectable semaglutide/tirzepatide through direct channels $199–299 (TrumpRx injectable $245 → $199 in 2028). Retatrutide (approved Mar 2028) is $449 self-pay; most plans exclude it for weight. List prices are nominal ($1,349 Wegovy unchanged). Employer coverage for weight management: 60% (2026) → 49% (2027) → 44% (2028). Nearly all employers still cover diabetes and, increasingly, the cardiovascular code. Gray market: the FDA finalised the 503B exclusion in 2027, but 503A 'personalised' compounding, 'research-use' retatrutide and cagrilintide vials, imported Indian generic pens ($40–90 delivered) and compounded 'monthly depot' semaglutide in microsphere suspensions regrew through offshore-hosted telehealth. Weekly injectables are still the largest by volume. Orals are ~35% of new starts. Monthly products are only legal ex-US or illicit.

on_market_classes: GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide, approved Mar 2028)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill 25 mg; Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
GLP-1/amylin combination, weekly injectable (CagriSema, approved Jan 2027 with modest uptake after losing to tirzepatide head-to-head)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: smoking/vaping cessation adjunct (Wegovy pill / oral semaglutide, approved Sep 2028 under a National Priority Voucher after two phase 3 trials showed ~1.8× continuous abstinence at 24 weeks vs placebo)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: gambling and compulsive-behaviour disorder: two RCTs (n≈150 and n≈220, 2027–28) show reduced gambling days and urges; no approval; Novo phase 3 in gambling disorder enrolling; New Jersey state pilot; 'impulse clinics' on telehealth also prescribe for compulsive shopping and pornography use
alcohol reduction: oral semaglutide phase 3 in AUD ongoing; widely prescribed off-label
microdosing / 'metabolic health' use by people without obesity, mostly cash and gray market
pediatric under-12 use off-label under specialist care
vaping cessation in 18–29s ahead of and alongside the oral label
drugs.pipeline_note: Approvals in window: CagriSema (Jan 2027, was under review) and retatrutide (BLA filed Feb 2027, approved Mar 2028; mean ~28% loss, label notes dysesthesia and a higher discontinuation rate). The monthly/implant driver is realised as far as the approval rules allow. MariTide (monthly, Amgen) was only 'in development' at the start of the window, so it cannot reach the US market by 2028. Its phase 3 read out in 2027 and its BLA was filed Mar 2028, with FDA decision expected 2029. China's NMPA approved a domestic monthly depot GLP-1 in Jan 2028. In the US, 'monthly' exists only as illicit compounded semaglutide microsphere depots. Amycretin is in phase 3 with readouts expected 2029. Survodutide was filed in 2028. Muscle-preserving adjuncts (bimagrumab + semaglutide) are in phase 3. Industry messaging has pivoted to 'quality of weight loss' (lean-mass share).

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the most common class effect and the leading cause of discontinuation. Higher with retatrutide at escalation.
Elevated with rapid weight loss; more visible with retatrutide's larger losses.
Absolute risk low; larger real-world datasets still do not confirm causality.

safety_ledger.effect: Lean mass (muscle) loss and bone-density decline
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Now a recognised population problem. Claims and DEXA cohorts (2027–28) find ~25–40% of lost weight is lean mass in users 65+. Hip-BMD declines of ~2–4% over two years exceed age-expected loss in continuous users, and sarcopenia diagnoses are rising in Medicare users with >15% weight loss.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA class labelling update (Jun 2028): warning on lean-mass and bone loss, baseline/periodic DEXA advised for 65+ and long-term users, resistance-training and protein counselling recommended. CMMI model requires DEXA for 65+ eligibility.

safety_ledger.effect: Fragility fracture in older long-term users
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Medicare-claims cohort (2028, ~1.9M users): hip-fracture hazard ratio ~1.35 among users 70+ on continuous therapy >2 years with >15% loss, vs matched non-users. Absolute excess ~2–3 hip fractures per 1,000 person-years. No excess under 60.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Included in the Jun 2028 class warning. Geriatric societies advise dose-tapering to maintenance once the weight goal is reached.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Meta-analyses suggest a small relative increase; absolute risk very rare.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: EMA 'very rare' label; FDA added a postmarketing adverse-reactions mention in 2027.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No causal association in further data.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia, apathy)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Pooled post-marketing and registry data put clinically noted apathy/anhedonia at roughly 0.5–1% of users, an 'uncommon' frequency. Patient surveys find 4–6% describing 'muted' enjoyment. Rates are higher on retatrutide and in people prescribed for compulsions. Dose reduction resolves most reports.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Jun 2028 label updates list apathy/anhedonia as an uncommon adverse reaction. No boxed warning. Clinics screen with a brief anhedonia scale at follow-up.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Real-world data settle closer to trial data. Roughly half to two-thirds of lost weight returns within 12–18 months off-drug. Regain is mostly fat, not muscle, which compounds the body-composition problem in cyclers.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Chronic-therapy framing; payers fund maintenance dosing.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Low protein intake and B12/vitamin D deficiency recurrent in older users; overlaps with the muscle–bone signal.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Counselling language in the 2028 class labelling; no testing mandate.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years; adolescents on decades-long therapy; repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Six years of follow-up now exist for the earliest RCT cohorts. Weight-cycling users show a less favourable lean/fat ratio after each cycle. Adolescent bone-accrual data are sparse.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Postmarketing requirements; NIH-funded adolescent bone-accrual cohort began 2027.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: After falling in 2026, FDA adverse-event reports tied to compounded or unapproved incretins passed ~4,500 cumulative by mid-2028. Cases include dosing errors with microsphere 'monthly depots' and retatrutide 'research' vials, and counterfeit pens in imported shipments.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: 503B exclusion finalised 2027; import alerts on Indian pen shipments; warning letters continue. Enforcement lags offshore-hosted telehealth.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Seen in phase 3 and post-launch; mostly mild and transient.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled at retatrutide approval; postmarketing study required.

food_and_beverage.state: GLP-1 households are ~30% of US households. US snack and confectionery volumes are ~3–4% below the 2026 baseline and sugary-drink volumes ~5% below, with value partly held by price and premium formats. Protein and 'muscle-support' callouts have overtaken 'GLP-1-friendly' labelling, partly because of the 2028 lean-mass warning. A counter-trend of 'real appetite' foods (full-fat, generous, unapologetic) is growing in urban premium retail.

alcohol.state: US spirits depletions are down a further ~4% across the window. The heavy-drinker cohort, which drives sales, is the most medicated. Off-label AUD prescribing and the new smoking-cessation label hit the drinking-and-smoking bar occasion. Low/no-alcohol is the only growing segment and does not offset the loss. Brewers consolidate SKUs.

restaurants.state: Traffic is roughly flat and check sizes premiumise. Smaller-plate menus are standard in suburbs. In Manhattan and Brooklyn, 'appetite dining' (large shared plates, tasting menus marketed as 'for the unmedicated') is a profitable niche among under-35s.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists keep shrinking through store closures (Torrid and DXL footprints down roughly a fifth). Mainstream brands recut around shoulders, arms and seat for a muscled ideal. 'Athletic fit' grows in menswear and womenswear.

fitness.state: Strength training is the growth market. Medicare-model counselling requirements, the lean-mass warning and the muscle ideal all pull the same way. Senior resistance classes, DEXA-scan studios and protein-coaching apps expand; YMCA and community centres contract with Medicare Advantage plans.

insurance.state: Employer weight-management coverage is down to 44%. Coverage now runs through diabetes, cardiovascular, OSA and MASH codes, which pushes up coding scrutiny and prior-auth disputes. Pharmacy trend has moderated to ~8% as unit prices fall. Retatrutide is widely excluded for weight. Medicare and Medicaid absorb the low-income tier.

pharma.state: The Lilly–Novo duopoly holds in the US with Lilly ahead (tirzepatide, retatrutide, Foundayo). US net price per patient-month is falling ~10–15% a year through negotiated channels while volume rises ~50%. Ex-US revenue is eroded by generics. Amgen is positioning MariTide as the adherence play.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Thin now reads as cheap and medicated rather than disciplined. Visible muscle, a big appetite and being 'natty' (gym slang now meaning off GLP-1s) signal scarcity: time, trainers, protein and the freedom not to need the drug.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Thinness is reachable through $0-copay public tiers at the bottom, $149–299 cash in the middle and $40 gray-market pens for the uncovered. Status has moved up a level. Affluent users still medicate at the highest rate (21%), but they pair low maintenance doses with trainers, DEXA scans and muscle, and talk about it less. The uncovered middle third is the group that can't afford either look.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Most GLP-1 households eat smaller meals. Among urban under-35s (Brooklyn, Austin, Los Angeles), eating a lot in public has become a display. 'Second helpings' dinner parties and mukbang-style restaurant content get read as proof of being unmedicated.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Dating-app profiles list 'natty' or 'on maintenance' the way they once listed smoking. A visible appetite counts as attractive among under-35s, while partners of compulsion-indication users report calmer but flatter households.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite is treated as both pathology and vitality. In medical settings it is a treatable signal, now formally including nicotine and informally gambling and shopping. In culture, wanting things openly is the new scarce good.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: Labelled as uncommon (~0.5–1% clinically noted apathy/anhedonia). 4–6% of users self-report muted enjoyment. Rates are higher among retatrutide users and those prescribed for gambling or compulsions. Clinics run a short anhedonia screen at dose escalation; dose reduction is the standard response.
interior_life.framing: Officially a side effect: uncommon, labelled, dose-dependent. For people treated for gambling, smoking or drinking, the same flattening is quietly described by clinicians and patients as part of how the drug works. Clinic language is 'the quiet', which is neutral on purpose.
interior_life.effect_on_work: No measurable labour-market effect. Anecdotes go both ways: commission salespeople and traders describe losing an edge, while shift workers and recovering gamblers describe steadier attention. No employer encourages or discourages use.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: Sports betting handle in New Jersey's pilot cohort falls sharply. Some musicians and comedians say publicly that they came off to 'get the hunger back', which feeds the 'natty' aesthetic. Fan culture around live sports and games carries a small but noticed share of people who watch without stakes.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Reduced libido and connection are reported by a minority. Couples-therapy referrals mentioning medication have become a recognised category. Most users report no change.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: Low but visible. Populist commentators on the left and right call the $0-copay tier and the gambling pilot 'sedating the poor'. Public-health officials answer with fracture and diabetes data. No organised movement exists.

state.regulatory_posture: Pro-access and fast on approvals: retatrutide on time, the smoking indication under a priority voucher. Enforcement against the regrown gray market continues but is outpaced. Safety posture tightened on bone and muscle with the 2028 class warning.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: Direct subsidy, no mandate. The CMMI Metabolic Health model gives $0 copay to Part D Low-Income Subsidy enrollees and adult Medicaid in 31 states + DC at a $219 negotiated price. New Jersey funds off-label gambling-disorder treatment from its problem-gambling fund. TrumpRx cash channel at $149–245.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Public coverage is conditioned on BMI/comorbidity, a baseline DEXA scan for 65+ and documented strength/protein counselling. Annual renewal requires an adherence attestation and a weight/BMD check. Employers condition coverage on diagnosis codes.
state.workforce_or_military: Little change. Armed forces require recruits who met body-fat standards on GLP-1s to show stability off-drug before accession. No workplace programmes.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: US brand exclusivity runs to ~2031–32 while generics are global. Personal importation from Canada and India is tolerated at small scale and targeted with import alerts at scale. China's monthly depot gives Beijing a talking point on 'next-generation' leadership. Manufacturers keep trading US price cuts for tariff relief.

events.event: Business Group on Health survey: employer coverage of weight-management GLP-1s falls to 49%, from 60%. Two large state employee plans and a major airline limit coverage to diabetes and cardiovascular codes.

FDA finalises exclusion of semaglutide, tirzepatide and liraglutide from the 503B bulks list. Within months, offshore-hosted telehealth sites are selling imported Indian pens, 503A 'personalised' semaglutide and 'research-use' retatrutide vials, some as compounded monthly depots.

CMS replaces the expiring Medicare GLP-1 Bridge pilot with a three-year CMMI Metabolic Health model at $219/month. Copays are $0 for Low-Income Subsidy enrollees and adult Medicaid in participating states; 31 states and DC sign on for 2028.
FDA approves Lilly's retatrutide for obesity at $449/month self-pay. The same month, Amgen files its BLA for once-monthly MariTide, two months after China approved a domestic monthly GLP-1 depot.

After a Medicare-claims study finds a ~35% higher hip-fracture risk in users over 70 on therapy for more than two years, FDA adds class warnings for lean-mass and bone loss with DEXA advice. Updated labels also list apathy/anhedonia as an uncommon adverse reaction.
FDA approves the Wegovy pill as an adjunct for smoking and vaping cessation. New Jersey's gambling-disorder pilot, paid for from sports-betting tax revenue, reaches 4,000 enrollees.

open_tensions: Public subsidy now reaches the poorest and oldest, and employers have left the middle. The uncovered middle third is the core gray-market customer, and the only legal fix the state has offered is cheaper cash.
The fracture signal sits in the same 65+ group the Metabolic Health model just enrolled at $0 copay. Nobody has decided whether to taper older users, add muscle drugs or narrow eligibility.
The flattening listed as an uncommon side effect is close to the therapeutic effect for gambling and nicotine. A state now pays for that effect, and a compulsion indication is in phase 3.

Monthly dosing exists legally in China and illicitly in US vials, while MariTide waits for a 2029 decision. Adherence-by-default is coming before anyone knows what years of continuous exposure, or repeated cycling, do to bone and reward.
still_true: No FDA-approved generic semaglutide or tirzepatide in the US; brand exclusivity still runs to roughly 2031–32.
Oral GLP-1 starter doses (Wegovy pill, Foundayo) still sell at $149/month through TrumpRx and manufacturer direct channels.
FDA's January 2026 removal of the suicidal-ideation warning from Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda labels stands.
Novo Nordisk and Eli Lilly remain the US incretin duopoly, with Lilly ahead on efficacy and orals.
Indian generic semaglutide still sells for roughly $8–48/month, a price gap every US politician cites.

prose.headline: Thin Is Cheap Now: how America's $0 diet drug made muscle, hunger and being 'natty' the last status symbols
prose.world_in_600_words:
By the end of 2028 about one American adult in six takes an incretin drug: roughly 45 million people, and nearly a quarter of adults have tried one. The drug is no longer a secret, and for more and more people it is no longer expensive. The way it is paid for has split the country into tiers.

At the bottom and at the oldest end the state pays. Medicare's Bridge pilot expired at the end of 2027 and was replaced by a three-year federal model that pays manufacturers $219 a month. Low-income seniors and Medicaid adults in thirty-one states pay nothing. The model comes with conditions. Anyone over sixty-five needs a DEXA scan before the first fill, and every renewal needs a note saying someone talked to the patient about lifting weights and eating protein.

Those conditions arrived just in time. In June a Medicare-claims study of nearly two million users found that people over seventy on the drug for more than two years broke their hips about a third more often than matched non-users. FDA put lean-mass and bone loss into a class warning. The fracture risk was the main story, but the agency also wrote something into the labels in the same update that patients had been describing for two years: apathy and anhedonia, as an uncommon side effect, usually fixed by lowering the dose.

The middle of the country has fallen out of coverage. Fewer than half of employers now cover these drugs for weight. Most still pay if the claim carries a diabetes or heart code, and doctors have become careful about which code they use. Everyone else pays cash, $149 for a starter pill and $199 to $299 for a maintenance dose, or buys outside the system. When FDA closed the big compounding pharmacies in 2027, the trade moved to offshore-hosted websites. They sell Indian generic pens for about forty dollars, vials of Lilly's newly approved retatrutide labelled 'for research use', and syringes of a monthly depot that no American regulator has approved. Around three and a half million people get their drug this way, and adverse-event reports have climbed again.

The drug's target has widened from hunger to wanting in general. In September the pill was approved to help people quit smoking and vaping. Gambling has no approval, but New Jersey pays for off-label treatment for four thousand problem gamblers from its sports-betting tax revenue. The clinics call the effect 'the quiet'. On the label it is a side effect. In the gambling clinic it is close to the reason for the prescription.

Culture has adjusted the way it always does when something gets cheap. In Brooklyn, Austin and Los Angeles, people under thirty-five have started treating thinness as a sign of a prescription. 'Natty', the old gym word, now means off the drug. Eating a lot in public has become a display, and restaurants sell big shared plates 'for the unmedicated'. Wealthier Americans are still the most medicated group, but they combine low doses with trainers and scans and talk about it less. Plus-size chains keep closing stores. Gyms, protein makers and senior strength classes grow, because a regulation, a fear of frailty and a new body ideal all point them the same way.

The economy has absorbed the change and kept going. Snack and drink volumes are a few points down and spirits are still slipping, while pharma volume rises even as the price per patient falls. Amgen has filed for a once-monthly injection, China has already approved one, and the American version exists only in unregulated vials. Nobody yet knows what a decade of continuous use, or repeated stopping and starting, does to bone or to desire.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Ray Castillo wakes at 5:40 in Paterson, takes the pill with four ounces of water, and waits the thirty minutes the way the nurse showed him. The bottle says NJ DIVISION OF GAMING ENFORCEMENT PILOT on a sticker over the pharmacy label. The cost to him is zero. His HVAC company stopped covering this kind of thing last spring.

In the truck he leaves the sportsbook app alone. It's still on his phone, two screens back. He doesn't feel like opening it.

At a job in Clifton the homeowner offers him a sandwich. He eats half and wraps the rest for later, and later he forgets it.

At four he calls the clinic for his check-in. The nurse runs the five questions. Does music still move him? Does he look forward to things? 'Some,' he says. She asks about the weekend. He says the Giants lost and he didn't mind. She writes something and keeps the dose where it is.

At home Marisol has made pernil. His daughter Ana is fifteen and comes in from the gym in a cutoff shirt, shoulders she didn't have last year, and takes a third plate. 'Natty,' she says, flexing at nobody. Her friend's mother is on the Indian pens, forty dollars a box, and Ana says the word 'Ozempic thin' like it means cheap.

They watch the Knicks. At the half Marisol takes his hand and studies him, the way she does now.

'You're here,' she says. It sounds like both a compliment and a question.

'I'm here,' Ray says. He means it. He also notices, from a distance, that the game doesn't matter to him at all.

least_plausible_claims.quote: smoking/vaping cessation adjunct (Wegovy pill / oral semaglutide, approved Sep 2028 under a National Priority Voucher after two phase 3 trials showed ~1.8× continuous abstinence at 24 weeks vs placebo)
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: the 2026 baseline had only anecdotal and observational nicotine evidence. Going to two completed phase 3 trials, a filing and an approval inside about 26 months is asserted, with no trial-start event in the candidate.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Pediatric: ~0.4% of all under-18s (about a quarter of those with obesity are aged 12+ with a prescription event).
least_plausible_claims.why: Magnitude: the parenthetical does not reconcile. 0.4% of all under-18s is roughly 290k children, about 2% of children with obesity, against the ~0.6% baseline for children with obesity, and the 'quarter' clause does not produce that figure.

least_plausible_claims.quote: compounded 'monthly depot' semaglutide in microsphere suspensions regrew through offshore-hosted telehealth
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: sustained-release microsphere depots are difficult formulation work. The candidate does not show how illicit compounders manufactured them within about a year of the 503B exclusion, so the leap is asserted.

rationale.badness: Harms are real but measured and labelled. These include a hip-fracture hazard ratio of ~1.35 in the 70+ group, 0.5–1% clinical apathy, ~3.5M gray-market users with a rising adverse-event count, and a stratified access ladder where the uncovered middle third falls through. A state paying for the 'quiet' in gambling patients and the 'sedating the poor' critique add autonomy and inequality costs. The harm is named, labelled and discussable (June 2028 label, DEXA screens), so epistemic badness is low and the overall world is a harder 2026, not a dystopia.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: Every driver is visible in fields and dated events: 17.1% adoption, price decline to $199/$219/$449, employer coverage 60→49→44%, nicotine and gambling indications, the muscle/bone class warning, a monthly product via MariTide filing and the China approval, gray-market resurgence, 'natty' inversion, $0-copay subsidy and niche anhedonia. mechanism: Most chains are shown, such as employer retreat leading to code-shifting and the 503B exclusion leading to offshore telehealth. The nicotine approval, the illicit microsphere depots and the DEXA requirement landing 'just in time' before the June study are asserted or convenient, per the quoted claims. magnitude: Adoption (17.1), ever-use (23.5), income thirds and the age-band average all sit inside the envelope and reconcile, as do the payer mix (44.8M), Medicare/Medicaid/LIS/NJ dollar arithmetic and the cycling arithmetic. Approvals respect the rules. Deductions: the garbled pediatric figure, public spending of roughly $13B/yr federal against CBO's ≥$35B for 2026–2034, and a bottom third below the middle third despite $0 copays.
rationale.generativity: The Ray Castillo day shows rather than explains: the sticker over the pharmacy label, the five-question anhedonia check, the forgotten half sandwich, Ana's 'natty' flex and Marisol's ambiguous 'You're here'. The world state implies many other scenes, including 'appetite dining', DEXA studios, impulse clinics, couples therapy, Indian pen deliveries and the NJ gambling pilot.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Pediatric: ~0.4% of all under-18s (about a quarter of those with obesity are aged 12+ with a prescription event).
least_plausible_claims.why: Magnitude: 2026 was ~0.6% of children with obesity (roughly 0.1% of all children). 0.4% of all under-18s would be a ~3-4x jump in two years. The parenthetical also implies about 25% of obese 12+ children are prescribed, which does not reconcile with 0.4% of all minors.

least_plausible_claims.quote: smoking/vaping cessation adjunct (Wegovy pill / oral semaglutide, approved Sep 2028 under a National Priority Voucher after two phase 3 trials showed ~1.8× continuous abstinence at 24 weeks vs placebo)
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism and magnitude: nicotine evidence in 2026 was only anecdotal and observational, with no phase 2 or phase 3 program. Two completed 24-week phase 3 trials plus an approval inside about two years, with no chain shown, is asserted rather than derived.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Medicare-claims cohort (2028, ~1.9M users): hip-fracture hazard ratio ~1.35 among users 70+ on continuous therapy >2 years with >15% loss, vs matched non-users.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: the Medicare obesity pilot began in Jul 2026, so few new obesity users could have more than 2 years of continuous therapy by mid-2028. With ~35% one-year persistence and >15% loss required, a cohort of ~1.9M users with a clean signal is hard to square with the starting world.

rationale.badness: The world is harder than 2026 but not dire. About 45M users, a measured hip-fracture excess of 2–3 per 1,000 person-years in older users, ~3.5M gray-market users, an uncovered middle third and 4–6% self-reported muted enjoyment are real but bounded. The state subsidises a compulsion indication, which the open tensions and 'sedating the poor' politics frame as an autonomy problem. Harms are labelled, screened and discussed (the Jun 2028 label, the anhedonia scale), so the epistemic score is low and the overall stays mid-range.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: every driver is traceable to fields and events.
